oncall-bot: :rotating_light: shift bridge — ongoing incident INC-2026-21 (embeddings rate-limit). Primary: Alex P. Secondary: Maria L. Root TS: 1778009123. Brief below, full notes and actions taken so far. PLEASE ACK if you take ownership for the next handoff window.

Alex P.: Quick summary — starting ~04:15 UTC we began seeing 429s from the embedding rate-limiter for requests to /v1/embeddings. Error rate peaked at ~12% of embedding requests (15m rolling). Affected parties: two EU mid-market customers (high QPS), one internal QA harness. Symptoms: 429s + elevated p95 latency for the embedding route. No data loss.

Alex P.: Impact classification: P2 (degraded service for a subset of customers). Customer-impact note: customer-redwood-eu reported API retries in production, engineering is coordinating with AE.

Maria L.: Observed correlation with a burst of small-batch streaming jobs from partner-integrations cluster between 04:10-04:18 UTC. These jobs were sending many short embedding calls (size ~32 tokens) which the token-bucket burst window didn't absorb.

Jit K.: Alerts firing: alerts/embeddings_rate_limit_high (firing since 04:16 UTC), dashboards: embeddings -> rate-limiter -> per-key throttles (link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/embeddings-rate).

Alex P.: Actions taken so far:
- Scaled embedding workers by +3 GPU instances in eu-west-1 (autoscaler triggered manual override).
- Increased token-bucket capacity for partner-integrations key (temp bump to 500) — manual change via `ratectl`.
- Enabled routing fallback for affected customers to `embed-lite-v1` (lower-cost, higher throughput) using the routing policy `fallback-embed-lite`.
- Added temporary prefix cache for repeated small inputs (TTL 30s).
- Opened ticket with infra to investigate redis key contention on `rl:emb:*`.

Alex P.: Short-term mitigation status: scaling appears to have reduced 429s by ~60% in the last 10m, but we still see occasional bursts. Fallback routing has prevented full outage for affected customers.

Maria L.: Outstanding risks: the partner job pattern can re-burst once it finishes; the embed-lite fallback degrades quality (notified PMs). If bursts resume, we may need a stricter per-customer throttle.

Sam O.: Ops note — we deployed a conservative patch to the rate-limiter yesterday that changed the refill window; might be exacerbating burst behavior. Reverting is non-trivial (risk to overall fairness).

Jit K.: Runbook pointers:
- Runbook: Embedding rate throttles: https://confluence.redwood/eng/runbooks/embeddings-rate-limit
- Quick playbook excerpt:
```
1) Identify offending key: `curl -s https://api.internal/rl/keys | jq .`
2) Increase token bucket for key: `ratectl set --key=partner:123 --capacity=500 --ttl=600`
3) Enable fallback routing: `rb route set --customer=partner:123 --profile=embed-lite-v1 --duration=30m`
4) Scale embeddings: `infra scale embeddings eu-west-1 +3`
```

Maria L.: Coverage/shift notes — I'm primary until 06:00 UTC but stepping into a 15-min call at 05:30. Alex, can you take primary from 05:25-06:05? If not, we need someone to cover.

Alex P.: I'm good to cover 05:25-06:05. I'll watch the dashboards. A few follow-ups I left in the incident ticket (INC-2026-21).

Maria L.: FYI I'm flagging customer comms for the two EU customers — AE notified and templated note prepared (waiting on confirmation about rollback vs stricter throttle).

Sam O.: Ops request: please capture `redis slowlog` for `rl:emb:*` keys before rotating nodes. I started collection to S3: s3://redwood-ops/incident-logs/INC-2026-21/redis-slowlog.log

Alex P.: Temporary customer routing command (run if 429s > 5% for 5m):
```
rb route set --customer=eucust-42 --profile=embed-lite-v1 --reason="emergency fallback" --duration=60m
```

Maria L.: Notes for next handoff (put in the ticket):
- Primary/Secondary mapping documented.
- Mitigations tried and timestamps.
- Current alerts and grafana panels.
- Link to redis logs and S3.
- Customer names + AE contact.

Jit K.: Coverage gap callout — there's a possible gap 07:50-08:10 UTC when oncall rotation includes overlap with weekly all-hands. If incident persists we should plan a temporary coverage swap.

sre-manager: Thx for the detailed notes. Action items for morning on-call: 1) Validate embed-lite quality impact with ML metrics, 2) Check redis cluster latency and consider node drains if hotspot persists, 3) Review yesterday's limiter patch in staging.

Alex P.: For whoever picks this up next: priority is to keep customer-facing error rate <1%. If we hit >3% sustained for 10m escalate to P1 (paging policy).

Maria L.: I'm ACKing the bridge and will paste this to INC ticket. I'll update the channel if anything changes during my call. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: (automated) New reminder scheduled: handoff-check at 05:20 UTC for transfer of primary duties.

Alex P.: Acknowledged. I'll take the handoff at 05:25. If anyone else picks up earlier ping me with `@Alex P.`

Sam O.: Adding a note: if you need to reduce noise but keep throughput, consider changing `sampling_window_ms` to 200 in the limiter config for short bursts. Deployed via `cfg apply limiter-config --env=prod`.

Maria L.: Last: I've added the Q/A from AE to the ticket (customer sensitivities). If we route to embed-lite please mention degraded embedding fidelity in the comms.

Alex P.: Signing off as current primary for the small overlap window. Leaving this thread open for updates.

(react: :eyes: by Jit K., :thumbsup: by Sam O.)
